Warriors defend their court to open the season with a win

By Lynelle Sarpong • November 8, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:14
Instaread

A consistent effort to keep points in the lead, along with a size advantage, led the El Camino College Warriors men’s basketball team to secure a 74-57 win in their home opener against the Oxnard College Condors on Wednesday, Nov. 4.

During the second half, the Condors fought back to put points on the board, going on a 9-0 run in the span of five minutes to cut the Warriors’ lead to four points.

However, an assist from Warriors guard Caleb Ortiz and a contested 3-point shot from guard Rocco Gaffoglio ensured their lead would stay for the remainder of the game.

The Warriors finished their game with 57.4% from the field goal, 53.8% from the three-point line, 21 turnovers, and 34 rebounds.

Warriors coach Robert Uphoff was excited that the team was able to come out victorious. He said it was a good building block for the team.

“We did some really good things, then we did some incredibly stupid things,” Uphoff said. “Just somewhat to be expected; we only got two returners from last year, and we know there’s going to be a learning curve.”

Uphoff said the forwards did a better job at executing compared to last game.

The second-year, Gaffoglio, played a patient game, letting the game come to him, and also having clutch shots down the stretch to help the team pull away.

“We had a real big problem with that last game where, as I would use the phrase, guys go rogue and start doing their own thing when nobody knows what they’re doing,” Uphoff said.

Guard Caleb Ortiz said he kept himself focused on the team’s assignment, which was to rush the Condors and to shoot consistent threes.

“We just had to get into our set, feed it to our bigs, and take it from there,” Ortiz said.

Ortiz helps his team by being a leader out on the court and reminding them that even if they mess up, there’s next play, or even celebrating with them after a made shot.

“It helps us with team bonding and chemistry in general,” Ortiz said.

Condors men’s coach Ron McClurkin said, “Sometimes you lose if you play well because some teams are just better.”

McClurkin said the team needs to work on listening and not just basketball skills. He also said that after cutting the lead down to four points, his player was walking back to defense.

Forward Derrick Martinez said that negativity is what keeps him focused on his goal and assignment for the game.

“I like being negative on the court; it really gets my teammates pumped up,” Martinez said.

Martinez said he wants to be more emotionally stable and available in the game. He believes he was shutting down in the game, which makes him mad. The team can work on being more together and on the same page, he said.

UP NEXT:

The Warriors’ men’s basketball team plays the Grossmont College Griffins on Wednesday, Nov. 11, at 5 p.m and the Desert College Roadrunners on Friday, Nov. 13, also at 5 p.m.

Both games are away.

Editor’s Note: This story was updated on Nov. 9 at 1:07 p.m. to correct captions and update game dates.
